narrative.overview: CodeEagle is designed as an authoritative, high-density developer instrument. It avoids the visual cliches of generic AI dashboards in favor of the disciplined restraint of premier developer tooling like GitHub Pull Request reviews, JetBrains IDEs, and Linear.
keyCharacteristics: High Information Density with compact 48px header and high-visibility viewport
Quiet Confidence with emerald green reserved strictly for actions and verified states
Micro-Precision Hairline Borders separating light commentary from dark code surfaces
Dual Typography with Inter for UI analysis and JetBrains Mono for code and metrics

rules.name: The Dual-Canvas Rule
rules.body: Code is always rendered on dark carbon surfaces (#171A19); analytical commentary, review findings, and administrative controls are always rendered on light mineral surfaces (#FFFFFF on #F5F7F6). Neither canvas invades the other.

rules.name: The Rarity Rule
rules.body: Emerald primary green (#0F9F6E) is applied to less than 5% of any view. Its visual energy is saved for moments of action (running a review) and resolution (successful patch verification).

rules.name: The Semantic Severity Rule
rules.body: Severity colors are strictly reserved for diagnostic findings and score badges. Never use red or orange for brand accents, decorative borders, or arbitrary icons.

rules.name: The Code-Only Monospace Rule
rules.body: Monospace typography (JetBrains Mono) is strictly confined to physical source code, line numbers, file names, commit hashes, and quantitative metrics. Explanations, review rationale, and user guidance must remain in Inter.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: All numerical indicators (overall scores, subcategory points, finding counts, line ranges) must render with tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) to prevent layout jitter during re-audits.

rules.name: The Hairline Border Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by crisp 1px borders, never by blurry drop shadows. Shadows appear only on elevated floating overlays (modals and slide-out drawers) to denote modal capture.

dos: Do maintain the strict Dual-Canvas distinction: dark #171A19 for code inspection, light #FFFFFF on #F5F7F6 for review analysis.
Do display engine source chips (AST vs AI) on every finding card to make provenance explicit.
Do use JetBrains Mono for all line numbers, file names, metrics, and code snippets.
Do keep line numbers clickable, smoothly scrolling and focusing the editor to the exact offending line.
Do provide instant feedback when code edits make existing analysis results stale (displaying Re-run Review warning state).
Do enforce single-file focus and compact density so developers can audit without scrolling through endless whitespace.
donts: Don't use neon gradients, playful emojis, or conversational chatbot dialog balloons in review findings.
Don't show ungrounded patches or raw LLM completions without SHA-256 validation and line verification.
Don't hide deterministic AST static analysis behind a generic 'AI thinking' spinner.
Don't use Monaco editor or heavy browser-side LSP bundles that degrade initial page load performance.
Don't use low-contrast text (ensure all secondary labels maintain at least WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast ratio against backgrounds).
Don't invent fake user testimonials or enterprise customer logos.
